Commentary.Commentary: The lesses said about the bowling the better. They were erratic and bowled all over the place. Run scoring was easy and no one was effective at all. They were plundered and put to the sword. In the end, they were ragged by the time the NZ skipper decided to end the innings. Now, 221 is the lead and Bangladesh are staring at defeat. They will have to bat really well and try to at least draw this game as a win looks hopeless from here. First of all there is the period of play this evening to be negotiated. Be back in a bit for that and the start of the 3rd innings...

394 runs in 73.1 overs! This is not even Test cricket you might think. But such was the domination of the Kiwi batting today. One man stood out, Ross Taylor. He made a double century, one of the best ever. He was involved in two massive stands, first with Williamson of 172 runs and second with Nicholls, of 216 runs. At the start of the day, the NZ skipper Kane and Ross both batted nervously as the ball was moving around. Taylor gave a couple of chances which were dropped when he was on 20. That was that though, no looking back post that. Taylor went on to smash a double century, Williamson missed out on a century battling with a shoulder injury and Nicholls got his 5th Test hundred. The runs flew thick and fast and New Zealand ended up with a lead of 221 runs.

200! Stand up where you are and applaud this innings! What an outstanding, marvellous effort this has been from Ross Taylor. His 3rd double hundred in Tests. He walked in at 8/2 and now it is 413/4. A length ball on middle, Ross comes down the line and pulls it away through square leg. It doesn not reach the fence but three can be taken. What an incredible innings, the adjectives are not enough. The celebration is not  a big one though, the helmet comes off and arms are raised to acknowledge the appreciation! The other important part about the double century is the strike rate. 200 off just 211 balls.

... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

Ross Taylor has reached 185 and is primed for a double century. On the other hand, Henry Nicholls is on course for his own hundred. The lead is 161 already and once these landmarks are achieved, New Zealand would love to have a go at the Bangladeshi batsmen once more this evening. The hosts can dictate terms and the visitors will have to dance to their tunes. No other way seems to be there now. Join us in about 20 minutes for the final session of play on Day 4!

As for the away side's bowling, the 2 dropped chances saw the whole idea change. The bowlers lost discipline and were taken to the cleaners by Kane and Ross, especially the latter as they scored at will. A run rate of more than 4.8 says a story on it's own. Does that mean the game is over? Quite possibly for Bangladesh, yes. Unless something dramatic happens and the Kiwis collapse in the next session. New Zealand on the other hand will look to continue with getting quick runs and have a sizeable lead. Meanwhile, the weather has played really nice so far with the sun even making an appearance. Hopefully it will stay like that for the rest of the day. What will happen on the field though? Return in about 40 minutes to find out...

What a session this has been for the hosts. 33.2 overs have been bowled by Bangladesh and 160 runs have come off them. Ross Taylor and Kane Williamson have absolutely bossed the visitors with the bat in the 2 and a half hours and have put New Zealand on course to what could be an unlikely victory in a Test which had 2 days washed out completely. The session began with the away side's bowlers doing really well and getting assistance off the pitch. They induced the edges and created the chances but none were taken. Ross Taylor was dropped twice and he made them pay. Kane Williamson and he stitched a 172-run stand before the skipper who had a shoulder injury fell without going on to make a ton. His partner, Ross Taylor though registered his 18th ton in Tests and is unbeaten there with Henry Nicholls who has joined him. Taylor was merciless and went for his shots and was especially brutal on Soumya Sarkar's bowling.

Short and wide outside off, Nicholls looks to cut the ball away but does not manage to put bat on ball.
Inside edge onto the pads! A length ball on middle, Taylor looks to defend but gets the edge onto his pads. A quick single is taken as the ball rolls next to the surface.
On the pads once more, worked towards mid-wicket but no run is available.
Bowled on the leg stump line, Taylor turns it towards square leg.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on to bowl.
A solid front foot defense to end the over.
Another one on the pads, worked towards square leg by Henry.
Flatter one on the pads, pushed towards square leg.
Henry Nicholls walks out at number 5.

OUT! Williamson has thrown it away here! He had a 100 for the taking there and Bangladesh have a wicket against the run of play. A flighted ball on middle and off stump line, was very full. Williamson looks to flick it on the leg side but the bat face closes too quickly and the ball takes the leading edge and goes back to the left of the bowler. Taijul takes an easy return catch and breaks the 172-run stand!
SIX! Kane's turn to show he can hit the big one too. A flighted one on middle, Williamson smashes this over the long on boundary after coming down the wicket.
Flatter one on the pads, Williamson works it towards square leg but fails to find the gap.
A solid front foot defense to end the 9-run over.
Short of a length just outside off, Taylor defends from the crease.
FOUR! This is looking all too easy for Taylor. A short length ball, served at 122 kph wide outside off. Ross cuts it hard through backward point for a boundary. A big hit shy of a ton now.
FOUR! Moves into the nineties now! A fuller one outside off, Taylor leans into this drive and times it past mid off really well. Super shot!
This time the ball is shorter and KW cuts it off the back foot to pick up a single to deep point.
Good length ball outside off, Williamson cuts it really late but the backward point fielder dives to his left and does really well to stop that one.
Williamson charges down the wicket to this flighted one and picks up a single to deep mid off.
Flatter one on middle, KW comes ahead and dead-bats this.
Kane has driven this fuller one to mid off.

Flatter and quicker on middle, Williamson brings his bat down in time after going on his back foot as he pushes it to the right of point. There was a single there but the skipper asks his partner to wait where he is.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Hurled in quicker on the pads, Taylor looks to flick it on the leg side but fails to put bat on ball. The ball goes off the pads towards the leg side for a run.
Cut away hard this time through point for a single as Rosco keeps strike.
Lucky for Taylor! A length ball outside off, too close to cut. Ross looks to chop it but gets an inside edge that bounces just past the stumps.
Hurled on a short length down the leg side, Ross can't make contact on his attempted pull.
Finally some calm as Taylor comes ahead and defends this ball on a length outside off.
FOUR! Slightly more square this time and a boundary to boot. Length ball on the pads, Taylor smashes this one over the head of mid-wicket and into the rope on a couple of bounces. Moves to 85!

SIX! That goes deep into the banks! A half-volley outside off and Taylor just stands tall and lifts the ball over long on. Huge! 150-run stand is up between these two. What a stand it has been, taking the game away from the Bangladeshis.
Fuller and quicker on off, driven to mid off by Williamson.
Flatter one on middle, defended from the crease by the skipper.
Flighted outside off, driven through covers to the left of the fielder in the deep. Couple of runs taken. Good running that from the two batsmen.
Shorter outside off, punched off the back foot to extra cover.
Fuller outside off, it is driven towards the mid off fielder.

Possible chance! Flies away from slip and all the way for four. Slower through the air and on a shorter length outside off, extra bounce too on that one. Williamson looks to cut it late but the ball flies off the edge and over first slip who barely moved. The ball runs to the rope. 150 comes up for the hosts.
FOUR! Smashed! A statement that! Fuller length outside off, Taylor frees his arms and lifts this ball over the head of mid on for a boundary.
Short and wide outside off, Ross cuts it late but gully dives to his right and makes a good stop.
Good length one on the middle stump line, Taylor pushes it to mid-wicket.
Some shape on that one. A length ball landing on off and seaming away late. Williamson adjusts late and drops the ball on the off side and picks up a run.
Fuller one outside off, driven hard through the covers for a single by Rosco.
On a length outside off, Taylor comes ahead and defends the ball towards the off side.
A good front foot defense from Kane to end the over.
Flatter and fuller on middle, Williamson pushes the ball to mid on and looks for a run but it went too quickly to the fielder.
A late cut from Taylor takes the ball away from backward point but the fielder in the deep comes around and stops the ball at just one run.
A flatter one on middle, Kane makes room before he pushes it to the left of deep cover for a single. He ran the first one hard but there was never more than one on that.
Shorter, wide outside off. Taylor rocks back and cuts it to deep cover for a single.
Flatter and quicker outside off, Taylor pushes it towards cover.
On a good length and outside off, the skipper does not bother to play at that.
Outside off, Williamson offers no shot.
On middle, the skipper blocks it well.
On a good length on off, Kane keeps it out.
Full on off, Williamson drives it to covers.
Length delivery outside off, Taylor cuts it towards third man. Ebadot Hossain does well to stop it with his right foot just before the ropes. The batsmen get three runs.
Slower through the air on middle and leg, KW prods ahead and dead-bats the ball.
Outside off on a flatter length, Kane pushes it from the crease to cover.
Flatter ball outside off, played really late by Williamson but he finds backward point.
Wide outside off, cut away for a single to deep cover.
Shorter in length on middle and comes slow to Taylor who is early into his pull and mistimes it towards mid-wicket.
Starts off with a flatter one on off stump line, pushed towards mid-wicket.
Taijul Islam comes into the attack now.
EDGE AND FOUR! Length delivery outside off, Williamson looks to drive but gets an outside edge. It goes over the second slip fielder towards third man for a boundary.
Outside off, Kane shoulders his arms to this one.
Back of a length on off, the skipper keeps it out.
On a good length on off, the skipper defends it off the back foot.
Short and outside off, Williamson looks to cut but misses it due to the movement on this one.
On off, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Fuller on middle and smashed for a boundary! Taylor comes ahead and then flicks it hard past mid-on to his right for four runs. 15 runs off this over, a massive one for the Kiwis.
On a length outside off, Taylor again looks to cut that one but gets an inside edge and the ball rolls towards slip.
Length ball just outside off, too close to cut hence the attempted cut sees the ball going towards cover.
SIX! THAT IS HUGE! Length delivery on middle, Taylor heaves it over mid-wicket for a biggie. A four followed by a six, maybe Taylor has decided that time is now ripe to attack.

EDGED AND FOUR! It was just over the keeper and out of reach from a diving Liton Das. Short and outside off, Taylor looks to cut but gets an outside edge as the ball had some extra bounce. It goes over the leaping Das for a boundary. Bangladesh having 0 luck here now.
Abu Jayed is back on. He starts off with one on a good length on off, Williamson taps it towards point for a run.
A length ball on off, defended by Taylor who presents a straight bat.

Loud shout for LBW! On a good length again on middle, Taylor looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad. Sarkar appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Probably height was the issue there. Good bounce from a length there!
On a good length on off, Taylor keeps it out.
On a good length on off, the skipper defends it towards point for a quick run.
Loud shout for lbw! On a good length on middle, Williamson looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad. The bowler appeals for but the umpire shakes his head. Probably height would have saved him.

Now it is fifty for Ross Taylor! The 31st Test fifty for him. Good innings from him, he was aggressive in the beginning and then settled down. He got a couple of chances but since then hasn't looked back. The delivery was full on middle, Taylor flicks it towards square leg for a run to get to the landmark.

DRINKS BREAK! The first passage of play on Day 4 has been dominated by the hosts. Early on, the Bangladesh bowlers did create chances but the fielders did not hold onto chances. Some edges flew wide. Now though, the two batsmen look in cruise control and are motoring along nicely. The visitors will hope for quick wickets now while the Kiwis will look to continue the good work. This is a long Drinks break because the physio is also out there again to have a look at Williamson who was in some pain. Meanwhile, Soumya Sarkar will bowl after the break.
On a good length on middle, the skipper blocks it off his back foot.

FOUR! 50 for Kane Williamson. 30th Test fifty for him. Great innings from him so far, he came in at a tough time and has bailed his team out along with Taylor. Coming to the ball it was a short delivery, Williamson pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary and brings up his half-ton. The deficit is also under 100 now.
On a good length on off, Kane keeps it out.
100 partnership between Ross Taylor and Kane Williamson. Short of a length delivery, Taylor pulls it towards short mid-wicket for a single.
Full on off, Ross drives it to covers.
On a good length and outside off, Taylor shoulders his arms to this one.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for the skipper. Length delivery on leg, Williamson flicks it towards fine leg for a boundary. 9 runs have come from the over. Good over for New Zealand.
Kane Williamson looked in some pain after playing the previous shot, grimaced a bit after it. He is continuing now though...
FOUR! Cracking shot. Short and outside off, Williamson cuts it through point for a boundary.
On a good length on leg, Williamson looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. There was no short leg there to catch it.
On a good length on off, the skipper defends it off the back foot.
On a good length and outside off, Williamson shoulders his arms to this one.
Short and outside off, Taylor cuts it through backward point for a single.
Fuller length ball outside off, driven by Kane to the cover fielder.
Around the wicket and shapes away after landing, Williamson leaves the ball well.
Short of a length on the hips, Ross works it towards the leg side and gets a single as the ball rolls towards mid-wicket.
Fuller length outside off once more, Taylor moves early, and then drives it a little to the left of cover for a couple.
Length ball on top of middle stump, defended by the batsman back towards the bowler.
Fuller length ball on the middle and leg stump line, Taylor looks to drive the ball through mid on but the ball goes off the outside half and towards backward point.
On a good length on off, the skipper defends it out.
Outside off, Williamson shoulders his arms to this one.
Short and outside off, Taylor cuts it through point for a run.
Dead ball! Short of a length ball on the hips, Taylor does not offer a shot. The ball goes off the sides and to the fence, but the umpire signals dead ball.
Full on off, the skipper drives it through covers. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it before the ropes. The batsmen get three runs.
Length delivery and outside off, Taylor cuts it towards backward point. The batsmen cross ends.
From around the wicket this time, Kane prods ahead a bit before defending the ball.
Short of a length, closer to the off stump this time. Williamson leaves the ball well.
Length ball well outside off once more, left alone by the Kiwi skipper once more.
Fuller length ball outside off and going away from the righty, left alone by the batsman.
Fuller length ball outside off, defended with soft hands by KW coming slightly ahead.
On a length outside off, left alone by Williamson.
The physio is out in the middle. Kane Williamson is receiving some treatment on the left shoulder that he was feeling yesterday as well. He is seen taking some pain-killers now.
Length delivery on middle, Kane flicks it towards square leg for a run. 7 runs have come from the over.
Back of a length delivery on off, the skipper defends it off the back foot.
Outside off, the skipper offers no shot.
Length delivery on leg, Taylor looks to nudge but gets hit on the pads. The batsmen take a run. The umpire gives it as a leg bye.
FOUR! Cracking shot. Full on middle, Taylor drives it straight past the bowler through mid on for a boundary.
On a good length and outside off, Williamson taps it towards point where the fielder dives to stop it but the ball goes through him. The batsmen take a run.
Ebadot Hossain is back on.

FOUR! Finds the gap this time! A fuller length ball outside off, almost yorker length. Taylor just redirects the ball wide of point to his right and finds the rope. A bad end to what was shaping up to be a decent over.
Length ball on the off stump line, Taylor looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside half towards the backward point fielder.
Left alone outside off by Ross this time.
Short and wide outside off, Taylor cuts it real hard but finds the fielder at backward point who makes a good tumbling stop.
On the middle stump line, pushed towards the leg side with soft hands.
Fuller length outside off, defended back towards mid off by Taylor coming forward.
On middle and leg, the skipper nudges it towards the leg side.
Length delivery outside off, the skipper taps it to short third man.
Outside off, the skipper lets it go.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Williamson plays a late dab towards third man. The slip fielder does well to stop it and saves runs for the team.
Length delivery on middle, Taylor flicks it towards square leg for a single.
On a good length on off, Taylor keeps it out.
Bowled at the hips, patted towards mid-wicket by Ross and picks up a single to end the 20th over.
On the leg stump line and aimed at the thigh pad, Taylor defends it back to the bowler.
Taylor looks to defend this ball outside off but the away movement causes him to be beaten. Good bowling!

Good effort to save one! A length ball outside off and Williamson dabs it onto the pitch. The ball bounces above the head of gully and goes towards the rope where the fielder chasing pulls it inside. 3 runs taken.
KW shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! The gap is threaded between the slips once more. A length ball outside off and Williamson dabs it really late and manages to pincer the gap between second and third slip. The ball reaches the rope.
On a good length on middle, Williamson looks to defend but the away movement squares him up. The ball goes off the outside half of the bat towards the off side. The batsmen take a single.
On a good length and outside off, the skipper leaves it alone.
Short and outside off, Williamson plays a late cut towards backward point. The batsmen get two runs.
Full delivery on middle, Taylor flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Some sawdust being brought and put on the landing area.
Full and outside off, Taylor drives it to mid off.
On a good length on off, Taylor offers a forward defense on that one.
Short of a length outside off, Kane looks to defend the ball but gets a thickish edge that runs wide of gully for a couple of runs. A good over from Mustafizur, but no luck there.
Dabbed by Williamson towards the right of second slip who dives to his right and makes a really good stop.
Oooh! Almost an edge! A length ball outside off with some away shape, Williamson was in two minds whether to play that or not. He decides to leave it really late.
Outside off, the skipper does not bother to play at that.
Peach! On a length outside off and moving away from the right-hander, Kane looks to defend but the shape makes his miss and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.

FOUR! Edged but safe! On a good length and outside off, Williamson looks to punch but gets an outside edge. It goes between the second slip and gully towards third man for a boundary. That was a great first ball from Rahman.
Mustafizur Rahman comes into the attack now.
Kept out of the back foot by Rosco to end this over.
Hurled down the leg side by Jayed, Taylor looks to come down the ground and flick it away through fine leg but fails to put bat on ball. This is confident batting though.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Oh guess who is making an appearance? The Sun!

FOUR! Edgy but Taylor will not mind. He is in the mood to go after everything here. A length ball wide outside off and moving away, Ross tries to cut but the ball goes off the thick outside edge and flies wide of the second slip fielder. The ball runs to the third man fence. The boundary also brings up the 50-run stand between these two, in real quick time!
Fuller one outside off, much better from the bowler. Taylor pushes it back towards mid off.

FOUR! Taylor's eyes lit up as soon as he saw that one! A length ball short and wide outside off, Ross cuts it hard through point and all the way to the rope. Poor start to this over from Abu after an amazing last over.
Back of a length delivery on off, Williamson plays it to point.
Short and outside off, Taylor cuts it towards point for a run.
Length delivery on middle, Williamson flicks it towards the leg side for a run.
FOUR! Nice shot. Short and outside off, Williamson cuts it through point for a boundary.
Bowls a bumper down leg, the skipper does well to duck under it.
Back of a length outside off, Williamson defends it off the back foot.

Taylor is certainly going to give chances if he plays this way. A length ball outside off, Ross goes for an expansive cover drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls back onto the surface. Really good over from Jayed, deserved a wicket!

Oooh! That could have so easily gone straight back to the bowler. A length ball on middle, Taylor pushes through the line and is early into the shot. The ball goes uppishly but just enough to the right of the bowler who has no chance on the followthrough. The batsmen pick up two runs till mid on runs and throws the ball back.
This time Taylor covers the line of the ball and pats it to the leg side.

DROPPED AGAIN! Would you believe it? At second slip this time. Jayed should have had his third in this over but does not yet. A length ball outside off and shaping away ever so late, Taylor looks to defend but gets the outside edge and the ball goes to the left of second slip where Shadman Islam dives low to take the ball but fails to hold on. Taylor is living a charmed life here!
Ross plays inside the line on this away swinging ball and is beaten.

DROPPED? Yes, it is! A sitter put down by Mahmudullah. A length ball outside off and shaping away, Taylor goes through with a cover drive and gets good timing on that one. It goes in the air though and straight to Mahmudullah at cover who puts his hand down to his left to take that ball but messes it. Lays down in disgust.
On the pads and tucked away fine on the leg side for a single. Taylor keeps strike.
Taylor was late on that one! A length ball outside off and jagging in, RT looked to leave that ball but decides to defend it in the end. He ends up getting it off the bottom half towards third slip.

Almost chopped on! A length ball just outside off, too close to cut but Ross goes through with the shot. Gets an inside edge but luckily for him it does not go on to the stumps and bounces above them before going to the keeper.
Another short length ball, good bounce on that ball on middle stump line. Ross defends it towards mid-wicket.
Short of a length on middle, defended towards mid-wicket by Taylor who stays tall.
Short of a length and wide outside off, Taylor looks to cut off the back foot going after that ball but fails to put bat on ball.
Outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Length ball outside off, pushed towards point by KW coming slightly ahead.

That has taken off! A length ball outside off and slight away movement, looks like it hit an indentation and bounced more as well as moved away. Williamson was nowhere near the ball and ends up playing inside the line.
Better line this time from Jayed, bowled on middle and slight away shape through the air. Kane covers the line and defends the ball.
FOUR! Shorter length ball at the ribs of Williamson. He glances it real fine on the leg side and manages to pick up a boundary. His first runs of the day.
Length delivery on leg, Taylor looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. It goes towards Watling where he fails to collect and gives an easy run. The umpire gives it as a leg bye.
The two batsmen come to the middle and have a look at the surface after the first two deliveries, especially at the indentations. Meanwhile, Abu Jayed to bowl from the other end.
On a good length on off, Williamson defends it off the back foot.
Starts with back of a length delivery on off, Williamson defends it out.
We are set to begin. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Kane Williamson and Ross Taylor are the overnight batsmen for the hosts. Ebadot Hossain will continue his over, 2 balls remain...

PITCH REPORT - DAY 4 - Light rollers have been used the previous days but this morning, the heavy roller has been used says Mark Richardson. Not much grass has been cut off and he comes near the surface and points at patches on the pitch due to the roller. There are slight indentations on the pitch as he shows us and reckons that the day could be a better one for the bowlers, even more than Day 3 with the overhead conditions cloudy as well.

The pitch quickened up quite a lot on Day 3 after initially being good to bat on. It is expected to continue assisting the pacers with lateral movement through the air and off the pitch. The overhead conditions are cloudy and overcast but the rain has stayed away so far. The forecast is for it to remain that way, we hope so too! The hosts will look to bat as long as possible while the visitors will look for early wickets. There could still be a result in this game, an exciting day in prospect provided the weather and light permits. Action is not far away...

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of this second Test between the Kiwis and the Bangladesh Tigers. After 2 rained out days on Day 1 and Day 2, we finally had play start on Day 3. Kane Williamson inserted Bangladesh in to bat first and then bowled them out for 211 in spite of a 74 from Tamim Iqbal. Wagner was the hero with the ball for them. When it was their turn to bat in the final session, only 11.4 overs were possible and they lost their two openers in the process. The skipper and Ross Taylor are out in the middle as of now and will resume batting on Day 4.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Thus, an engrossing day's play. One would believe that with more than 2 days being washed out, this game would surely be a draw but seeing the pace of the game today, anything can happen if weather permits on the final two days of the game. Monday will be Day 4 of the Test and the forecast does seem clear. Hopefully, play will start on time and we can have an uninterrupted game. There will be an early start on Monday as well. Join us at 1030 local (2130 GMT, Sunday night) for all the action. Till then, take care and cheers!

It has been a quick-paced day for sure though. A total of 72.4 overs were possible on Day 3. Bangladesh on the back of yet another fifty from Tamim Iqbal managed to put on board 211. They will be disappointed though because they did have more than a decent start on a green wicket where they were inserted to bat on. The wicket quickened up as the day passed and eventually wickets fell in bulk towards the latter half of the innings. Wagner with 4 and Boult with 3 were the chief tormentors of the away side. Post Tea, when the Kiwis came out to bat, the visitors' bowlers used the pitch and overhead conditions to best effect. The ball moved around and they have managed to send back both the in-form openers, both wickets went to Abu Jayed. Ross Taylor and Kane Williamson were out there in the middle, the former being in aggresive mode, when the rain decided to come down after being away all day. That was the final bit of play as the umpires decided no further play would be possible.

Update 1745 local time - Sorry guys! Bad news! Play has been abandoned on Day 3. The drizzle was persistent and though it was light, it was enough for the game to be called off on the third day. The light also seemed to be fading a bit. The umpires strolled out for an inspection a little while back and decided that we have had our final action of the game for today.

Update 1725 local - The rain is persisting as of now and we continue our wait for it to stop. Things starting to look bleak now in respect to whether we may have any further play. Waiting for official word though...

Slight drizzle here and the umpires come in the middle to have a discussion. And.... we are going off! The Hessian comes on first to cover the pitch, followed by the rest of the covers for the square. The umpires are not hurrying off exactly, suggesting they're not too worried and it could be a passing shower. Hope it is!
Outside off, Williamson lets it go.
Length delivery on off, Taylor defends it towards point and takes a quick run.
FOUR! Good shot. Short of a length delivery, Taylor pulls it past wide mid on for a boundary.

FOUR! On a good length and outside off, Taylor looks to guide but gets an outside edge. It goes towards third man for a boundary. Ross Taylor survives and it could have been a catch but luckily for him the ball goes in the gap.
FOUR! Such deft and soft hands from Williamson. A length ball outside off, Kane plays it late and dabs it between the slip and gully fielders. The ball runs fast and reaches the rope easily.
Length ball on off stump, pushed through mid-wicket for a single by Rosco.
Short of a length outside, Ross defends it from the crease.
On the pads, Taylor looks to turn it away through square leg but the ball goes off the pad and the batsmen pick up a couple of leg byes.
Fuller length ball outside off, mistimes his drive back towards mid off.
Good stop! A length ball outside off, Taylor cuts the ball hard into the ground. Tamim at backward point dives to his right and makes a good stop, saving a sure boundary.
FOUR! Nice shot. Williamson flicks it towards fine leg for a boundary. 6 runs have come from the over.
On a good length on middle, Taylor looks to defend but gets a leading edge towards the leg side. The batsmen take a run.
Bowls a yorker on off, Taylor does well to dig it out.
Length delivery on middle, Williamson flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Outside off again, the skipper shoulders his arms to this one.
On a good length and outside off, Williamson lets it go.

FOUR! Rocket start for Taylor here. A fuller length ball outside off once more, Ross is a long way out to cut down the movement. He drives it hard through point for a boundary. Two fours and a wicket off the over.
Well outside off and coming slightly inward, left alone by Taylor.

FOUR! Another good start, this time it is from the new batsman. The ball is full outside off and Taylor leans into the drive, puts it into the gap through covers. Finds the fence on his first ball to get off the mark.
Ross Taylor walks in at number 4.

OUT! Caught at cover! New Zealand have lost their second! Bangladesh are surely making they're still in this game with early wickets. A fuller length ball outside off and shaping away, Raval was leaving these all along but this one was slightly closer to the off pole more than the previous ones. He goes for the drive but cannot keep the ball down and gives an easy catch to Soumya Sarkar at cover. The hosts are two down with under 10 on the board. Brilliant start from the visitors, just what they would have wanted. Abu Jayed has his second and is ecstatic.
On a good length on off, Raval defends it off the back foot.
On a good length and outside off, Raval leaves it alone.
On a good length on off, the skipper blocks it off his back foot.
On a good length on middle, Williamson looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Length delivery on middle, Raval flicks it towards the leg side for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Raval lets it go.
BEATEN! On a good length on off, Raval looks to defend but misses it due to the away movement on this one.
On a good length on off, Raval defends it off the back foot and gets hit in the right glove.
Outside off, Williamson does not bother to play at that.
On a good length on middle, the skipper keeps it out.
On a good length on off, Williamson looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a good length and outside off, the skipper offers no shot.
On a good length on off, Williamson looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards gully where it fell short of the fielder.
Full on off, Williamson drives it to covers.
Outside off, Raval lets it go.
On a good length on middle, Williamson tucks it towards mid-wicket for a run. The skipper is off the mark.
Full on off, Williamson drives it to mid off.
On a good length and outside off, Williamson shoulders his arms to this one.
Length delivery on middle, Raval flicks it towards square leg for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Raval looks to defend but gets beaten due to the away swing on this one. There was seam movement also.
Kane Williamson walks in at number 3.

OUT! This time it takes the edge and is pouched easily by Das. The last ball went past the outside edge but this time the knick is induced. A length ball just outside off and shaping ever so slightly away. The length entices the drive from Latham but the movement ensures the edge is taken and Liton makes no mistake. That is the early breakthrough Bangladesh were looking for. Tom Latham walks back cheaply, a rare failure for him.
Peach! Outside off and shaping away, moves just enough to go past the outside edge of Tom who was looking to defend.

Loud appeal but no reaction from the umpire! Lovely ball that was, looked pretty close as well. A length ball landing on middle from around the wicket, the ball shaped away in the end to beat the bat of Latham who was trying to defend the ball. It goes on to hit the thigh pad of Latham in front of the stumps. Height seems to be the issue there. The replays roll in and they too say that the ball would have gone over the stumps.
Fuller one on middle, driven back to the mid off fielder.
Bowls this wayward! Way outside off on a length and more away movement as well. Latham lets the ball go.
FOUR! That is a gift for the batsman. Fuller one on the pads, Latham flicks it away beautifully past mid-wicket and picks up a boundary. The first one of the innings.
Bowls a bouncer, Raval does well to duck under it. A maiden over from Ebadot Hussain.
Length delivery on middle, Raval flicks it to the leg side.
On a good length on middle, Jeet defends it out.
Outside off, Raval lets it go.
On a good length and outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to this one.
APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! On a good length on middle, Raval looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Probably it is missing leg.
On a length on top of off stump, defended off the back foot towards point by TL. Second maiden on the trot.
On the middle stump line, Latham works it towards mid-wicket and looks for a single but the fielder there dives to his right and makes sure no run is taken.
Once more well outside off, left alone.

Close to the off stump but you will have to say well left. Latham comes ahead with a big stride to this ball landing on a length outside off and coming in slightly. The batsman covers the line of the ball and shoulders arms to it.
